additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food in a discrete period while experiencing a sense of loss of control over eating, occurring at least weekly for several months and causing significant distress. Unlike bulimia nervosa, binge episodes are not regularly followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative misuse, or extreme exercise. The disorder often emerges in late adolescence or adulthood and may fluctuate with stress, dieting attempts, weight stigma, or mood disturbances, frequently co-occurring with anxiety or depressive symptoms. Many patients initially present in primary care, weight-management, or psychotherapy settings, often reporting shame and secrecy around their eating before fully recognizing the pattern as a distinct disorder.

patient.stressor: About a year ago, Ganelle was promoted to a senior designer role and took on several high‑profile museum and nonprofit branding projects at once, priding herself on meticulous control over every detail. To meet overlapping deadlines and stay competitive in her studio, she began regularly working late into the night in her small Boston apartment, skipping sit‑down meals and relying on delivery apps and prepared foods while she refined layouts and experimented with generative AI. Over roughly 10 months, her solitary, over‑booked schedule blurred the line between work and personal time, and she noticed that her previously deliberate approach to food was being replaced by chaotic, late‑night eating sessions that left her feeling out of step with her carefully curated life. The pattern became impossible to ignore when she started turning down social invitations and even long‑planned hiking and museum days because she felt drained and preoccupied with these episodes, leading her to seek psychiatric help after a colleague casually suggested she might be "using food the way some people use alcohol" to get through projects.
patient.chief_complaint: “When I’m alone working late, I start eating and it feels like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating until it’s over.”

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On a lot of these late nights, I’ll order enough takeout for three people—like two entrees, extra sides, dessert—and then still go through half a family-size bag of chips and whatever’s in my freezer, all within an hour or two while I’m tweaking fonts on my laptop.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it’s like a switch flips and I’m just shoveling food in while I keep working, telling myself to stop but feeling weirdly detached, like I’m watching my own hands keep reaching for more even though I don’t want to anymore.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat so fast during these episodes that I barely chew—just bite, swallow, next bite—until I suddenly realize I’ve finished everything in front of me and can’t even remember what it tasted like.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: I don’t stop until my stomach is so tight and bloated that I have to lean back in my desk chair and hold my breath for a second because it hurts to sit up straight.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: Sometimes I’ll finish a normal dinner, feel physically full, and then an hour later I’m back in the kitchen loading up another plate or opening more apps to order food even though my body is giving me zero hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I’ve gotten into this habit of waiting until my roommate’s door is shut and the lights are off, then I’ll quietly bring all the food into my room and eat it on the floor so she doesn’t see the pile of containers and judge how much I’m putting away.

add_requirements.binge_frequency: For most of this past year, I’ve had at least one of these out-of-control late‑night eating blowups every week, sometimes more often when deadlines pile up.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve started turning down weekend plans and even leaving some work to the last minute because I feel so sluggish, ashamed, and mentally foggy the day after a binge that I just want to hide in my apartment.
add_requirements.duration: This whole pattern of late‑night, out‑of‑control eating has been going on for about ten months, basically since a few months after I took the senior designer role and all the big projects hit at once.
